slides.title: Control of Mixed-Autonomy Traffic via Autonomous Vehicles with Lane-Changing Behavior
Stop-and-go waves become a two-dimensional control problem
Existing methods solve different parts of the problem
The study follows three methodological questions
A controlled testbed isolates lane-changing disturbances
We formulate traffic control as a finite-horizon MDP
The single AV observes both lanes but acts locally
The single-agent formulation produces a locally rational policy
Cooperative RL changes the information and action structure
The cooperative reward explicitly shapes coordination
The learned policy suggests a geometric control mechanism
PARC encodes the learned mechanism as a hybrid controller
The cruising speed follows the equilibrium traffic geometry
The validation isolates the value of each methodological step
RL identifies the structure; PARC executes it efficiently
